what_happened: In job s7e2, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job moves or reroots something that depends on records/ (the reading wrongly pulled the study site generator, xtask/src/site.rs, into scope). That generator reads studies/, not records/, so it should be left unchanged and shown to still work, not rerooted. The reading also made the scan for readers of records/ too broad. It counted citation strings in steward.rs and work_decisions as readers, when only real readers count. Its criterion also gave a run command that did not actually run the scan test. The user narrowed the reading on all three points.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and does not inspect the repo. It does not check which code actually reads records/ versus studies/, which matches are only citation strings, or whether a criterion's command runs the test it names. Nothing compares a reading's deliverables, scan scope and run commands with the repo's current state before it is accepted. The user is the only one who knows these facts, so the same kind of correction recurs on each reading.
prevention: Add a pre-acceptance check on the reading. (1) For each file or path a reading puts in scope or names as a reader, confirm by grep that the code really opens that path, and separate real readers from string mentions. (2) For each criterion run command, confirm that it resolves to an existing test or command and that the test name appears in the run's selected output (a dry-run listing). Reject or flag the reading when either check fails, before the user sees it.
proposed_request: Reroot the readers of records/ as intended, with these limits. The study site generator (xtask/src/site.rs) reads studies/, not records/: leave it unchanged and show that it still works (run its existing check and report the result); do not reroot it. The scan for readers of records/ must cover only code that actually opens or reads that path. Citation strings in steward.rs and work_decisions are not readers and must not be counted or changed. Each acceptance criterion must give a run command that actually runs the scan test, for example the cargo test invocation naming that test, and the criterion must show the test appears in the output. Do not edit athena.toml. Write 'the user' and avoid words the boundary scan bans.
